coverage.assessment: Two links are cut: the bridge from 'a party of his own' to the circle's formative influence, and the circle's tie to the statesman system that chapter 005's bargain story relies on. The tools passage also lost its stated payoff.
'From the one as from the other' dangles because the Boston Whig comparison was cut. 'These four gentlemen' still squares with 'numbered only three' plus Mr. Adams.
The chapter has no performed dialogue. The father's reported complaint about punctuation is correctly attributed.

The poise passage loses its second 'No doubt' hedge, the risk the plan named. The school section loses 'the boy had nothing to complain of.' 'Cold' stays attributed to the critics and is balanced by the father's laugh.
The old man's irony at the children's blindness to their father is cut. The Sumner bond carries no premature hint of rupture, and no London achievements are stated.
Signature paradoxes are trimmed: 'abused... for his judgment,' 'So they were' with its turn, and the ant/elephant deflation. Double hyphens, aphorisms and the verbatim lines survive.
Without its reversal, 'So they were' now reads as plain endorsement of Puritan moral superiority. That changes the argument about why the Puritan could not change.
All five local endpoints and their partner endpoints (006, 009, 010, 007, 027) survive in the revised texts.

dependencies.assessment: All four tools are listed, with Mathematics first. Chapter 006 keeps the mathematics 'alphabet' payoff.

evidence.quote: the facile use of only four tools: Mathematics, French, German, and Spanish.
he needed to read mathematics, like any other universal language, and he never reached the alphabet.

dependencies.assessment: The bond is closer than blood and heroic, with no hint of rupture. Chapter 009 keeps the 'friend in power' rule.

evidence.quote: The relation of Mr. Sumner in the household was far closer than any relation of blood.
the rule that a friend in power is a friend lost.

dependencies.assessment: Absence of self-consciousness and steadiness 'even under great pressure' survive locally. The London test pays off in chapter 010.

evidence.quote: absence of self-assertion or self-consciousness--the faculty of standing apart without seeming aware that he was alone
his mind and temper were as perfectly balanced; not a word escaped; not a nerve twitched.

dependencies.assessment: The Marx exception and the coal/steam figures are kept. Chapter 007 keeps Marx 'waiting for him.'

evidence.quote: No one, except Karl Marx, foresaw radical change. What announced it?
he had no idea that Karl Marx was standing there waiting for him

dependencies.assessment: The vanished instinct and the 'many efforts to recover it' line are kept without anticipating the dynamo. Chapter 027 keeps the prayer.

evidence.quote: The religious instinct had vanished, and could not be revived, although one made in later life many efforts to recover it.
Before the end, one began to pray to it;

findings.claim: The first draft kept two lines the revision cuts. One is 'They abused Charles Francis for his judgment.' The other is the second 'No doubt' sentence, in which the self-conscious children were too ignorant to see how rare the model was ('A coarser instrument would have impressed them more'). In the revision, the aphorism about the world's love of imbalance follows the first hedge directly.
findings.counterevidence: The first 'No doubt' survives, and so do V2, V3 and the full trait list.

evidence.quote: No doubt, too, that even his restless-minded, introspective, self-conscious children who knew him best were much too ignorant of the world
A coarser instrument would have impressed them more.
was not maintained by nature without a sacrifice of the qualities which would have upset it. The world never loved perfect poise.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's second 'No doubt, too...' sentence and 'A coarser instrument would have impressed them more.' Optionally restore 'They abused Charles Francis for his judgment.'
findings.plan_relation: Required. The plan's risks call out the 'No doubt...' qualifications.
findings.reader_effect: The retrospective self-indictment that makes the praise credible and ironic is lost, and the father's case reads closer to plain eulogy. The plan named exactly this risk.
findings.title: Poise passage loses its second 'No doubt' hedge and the judgment paradox

findings.claim: The source follows 'So they were' with the point that the Puritan could not be convinced moral standards had nothing to do with it. The revision cuts that sentence, so 'So they were' runs straight into Henry's churchly nature.
findings.counterevidence: The stamp-of-1848 argument and 'it was easy' for outsiders still imply that change was required.

evidence.quote: So they were. He could not be convinced that moral standards had nothing to do with it
So they were. He could not be convinced that moral standards had nothing to do with it
better than those of his successors. So they were. Nature had given to the boy Henry a character

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's sentence beginning 'He could not be convinced that moral standards had nothing to do with it...'
findings.plan_relation: Required. The essentials name 'So they were' as part of the Puritan-bias argument.
findings.reader_effect: Adams's turn is that the Puritan was right about morals and wrong that morals mattered. Without it, the line reads as unqualified agreement, and the reason for the old nature's resistance to change goes with it.
findings.title: 'So they were' loses its dry reversal

findings.claim: The revision reduces the section to the Webster–Everett succession. It drops 'each profession were a church,' 'Sumner aspired to break the succession, but not the system,' and the Mount Vernon group as 'statesmen, not politicians.' The first draft had kept all three.
findings.counterevidence: 'This sort of world' in paragraph 15 still resolves to the professional system, and chapter 005 remains readable on its own.

evidence.quote: The little group of men in Mount Vernon Street were an offshoot of this system; they were statesmen, not politicians
The little group of men in Mount Vernon Street were statesmen, not politicians; they guided public opinion, but were little guided by it.
Thus Boston chose Daniel Webster, and Edward Everett held the rank in regular succession to Webster.
With this bargain Mr. Adams and his statesman friends would have nothing to do

findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'Charles Sumner aspired to break the succession, but not the system' and the first draft's 'statesmen, not politicians' sentence.
findings.plan_relation: Required. The essentials list 'government... by the best' and the Webster succession. The cross-chapter link is a planning omission.
findings.reader_effect: The section no longer explains the boy's own world, only Webster's. Chapter 005's revision relies on 'his statesman friends' recoiling from machine politics, a contrast this chapter no longer sets up.
findings.title: Mount Vernon circle cut loose from 'government by the best'

findings.claim: In the source, 'the one... the other' refers to the Boston Whig debates and John Adams's controversies. The first draft cut the Boston Whig sentence, and the revision keeps the residue unchanged.
findings.counterevidence: The two editing projects mentioned earlier in the paragraph can serve loosely as the pair.

evidence.quote: Yet the discussions in the Boston Whig were carried on in much the same style as those of John Adams and his opponent
The boy got as little education, fitting him for his own time, from the one as from the other
The boy got as little education, fitting him for his own time, from the one as from the other

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the source's 'Yet the discussions in the Boston Whig were carried on in much the same style...' sentence before 'The boy got as little education.'
findings.plan_relation: An authorized compression that leaves a dangling residue.
findings.reader_effect: The reader has to guess what is being paired. The joke's sting is also lost: the newspaper the boy hears debated is as dull as his great-grandfather's prose.
findings.title: 'From the one as from the other' has lost its pair

findings.claim: The revision cuts the sentence saying the political party 'became a chief influence in the education of the boy Henry in the six years 1848 to 1854' and shaped his plastic character. Paragraph 10 now opens straight on the group of men.
findings.counterevidence: 'Set up a party of his own' immediately precedes the paragraph, so the link remains inferable.

evidence.quote: This political party became a chief influence in the education of the boy Henry in the six years 1848 to 1854
violently affected his character at the moment when character is plastic
The group of men with whom Mr. Adams associated himself, and whose social centre was the house in Mount Vernon Street

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's opening sentence of paragraph 11.
findings.plan_relation: A planning omission. Not listed as optional, and it carries the chapter's time frame.
findings.reader_effect: The causal hinge between the father's middle path and the Mount Vernon circle disappears. So does the only anchor for the chapter's 1848–1854 span.
findings.title: Paragraph linking 'party of his own' to the boy's formation dropped

findings.claim: The revision cuts the clause that the sons would pay for the pilotage 'with their lives wasted on battle-fields or in misdirected energies.' The first draft kept it.
findings.counterevidence: The essential contrast between the father's channel and the sons' ocean, and between the two generations, is intact.

evidence.quote: it mattered little to his success whether they paid it with their lives wasted on battle-fields or in misdirected energies and lost opportunity
The task done, he might be content to let his sons pay for the pilotage
while for himself an unknown ocean lay beyond. The generation that lived from 1840 to 1870

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's two sentences beginning 'His father's business in life...'
findings.plan_relation: Optional tradeoff. The essential core is kept.
findings.reader_effect: The metaphor keeps its clear channel and unknown ocean but loses its dark edge and the shadow of the coming war.
findings.title: Pilotage loses its bitter cost clause

findings.claim: The first draft cut 'the boy had nothing to complain of' and the following 'never complained' lines. The revision then dropped the rote-learning reason ('compelled to learn by memory'), so 'His memory was slow' arrives without context. It also dropped the stated payoff of the four tools ('With these, he could master...').
findings.counterevidence: V7 and V8 are verbatim, and 'positive gain' and 'time thrown away' convey the core.

evidence.quote: He hated it because he was here with a crowd of other boys and compelled to learn by memory a quantity of things that did not amuse him.
With these, he could master in very short time any special branch of inquiry, and feel at home in any society.
The dislike of school was so strong as to be a positive gain. His memory was slow, and the effort painful.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the 'compelled to learn by memory' sentence and the 'With these, he could master...' sentence.
findings.plan_relation: Optional tradeoff. The essentials are kept.
findings.reader_effect: Hatred of school reads as a grievance against a bad school rather than against method, and the tools list loses its rationale.
findings.title: School grievance and tools passage thinned

strengths: All eight verbatim passages survive intact, including the V5 hyperbole and the V6 Unitarian irony.
The critics' 'cold' charge stays attributed and is balanced by the father who 'laughed over a witticism till he choked.'
The optional cuts are clean: the quatrain's lead-in now ends in a full stop rather than a colon, and the woolsack and Evarts material go together.
The vanished-religion paragraph keeps its full arc, from the forms of worship through the chasm image to Emerson's 'naif' protest.
summary: The revision is coherent and keeps every essential unit, all eight verbatim passages, the continuity checks and all five dependencies. It goes further than the first draft, though. It strips several of Adams's hinge sentences: the reversal after 'So they were,' the second 'No doubt' in the poise passage, the battlefield cost of pilotage, and the 'statesmen, not politicians' tie between the Mount Vernon circle and government by the best. The revision appears to run below the 3,000-word target, so small restorations look affordable. One first-draft residue ('from the one as from the other') lost its antecedent. Nothing rises to must_fix.
